VitalSync – Remote Patient Monitoring
System

Introduction

VitalSync is a healthcare-focused web application designed for real-time remote
monitoring of patients using IoT devices. It enables doctors to track vital signs and
respond to critical conditions efficiently.

Application Overview

The platform tracks heart rate, oxygen levels, temperature, and activity patterns with
real-time updates and dashboards.

Frontend Architecture

The system follows a layered architecture including presentation, state management,
service, and visualization layers for efficient rendering and data handling.

Core Features

Real-time monitoring, alert systems, patient dashboards, historical data visualization, and
role-based UI rendering.

Performance Optimization

Optimized using lazy loading, throttling, memoization, and efficient rendering for large
datasets.

Security

Implements secure authentication, encrypted communication, and role-based access
control.

Conclusion

VitalSync ensures reliable and scalable healthcare monitoring with an intuitive frontend
system.

AI-Driven Developer Task Assignment

Deep Learning Integration in Workflow Orchestrator

Field 
Details

Project Title 
AI-Driven Developer Task Assignment using Deep Learning

Subject 
Artificial Intelligence

Project Type 
Integration Module (Workflow Orchestrator)

Technology Domain 
Deep Learning, NLP, Recommendation Systems

Academic Year 
2025 – 2026

Team Members 
Prince Thakarar(23BCP500D), Meet Joshi(23BCP502D)

1. Introduction

In modern software development, assigning the right task to the right developer is a critical challenge 
faced by project managers. Incorrect assignments lead to delays, poor quality output, and team 
inefficiency. The existing Workflow Orchestrator project automates and manages development tasks, but 
currently relies on manual task assignment.

This synopsis proposes the integration of a Deep Learning (DL) model into the Workflow Orchestrator 
that intelligently recommends the most suitable developer for any given task. By analyzing a developer's 
past experience, skill set, performance history, and current workload, the system will provide data-driven 
assignment suggestions that improve team productivity and project delivery.

2. Problem Statement

Current task assignment in workflow systems is entirely manual and depends on the project manager's 
subjective judgment. This leads to several challenges:

• 
 Mismatch between developer skills and assigned tasks, resulting in poor quality output. 
• 
 Overloading of certain developers while others remain underutilized. 
• 
 Inability to consider all relevant factors (skills, workload, past performance) simultaneously. 
• 
 No learning mechanism to improve assignments over time based on outcomes.

recommendations automatically.

AI-Driven Developer Assignment | Workflow Orchestrator Project

3. Objectives

• 
To build a Deep Learning model that recommends the best-fit developer for a given task. 
• 
To process task descriptions using Natural Language Processing (NLP) to extract required skills 
and complexity. 
• 
To create rich developer profiles based on historical task data, skills, and performance metrics. 
• 
To integrate the recommendation engine seamlessly into the existing Workflow Orchestrator. 
• 
To provide a feedback loop so the model continuously improves from new assignment 
outcomes.

4. Proposed System

4.1 System Overview

The proposed system is a recommendation engine embedded within the Workflow Orchestrator. When 
a new task is created, the system automatically analyzes the task details and developer profiles, then 
suggests the most suitable developer. The project manager retains final authority to accept or override 
the suggestion, and this feedback is fed back into the model for retraining.

•

•

• 
Manager override capability to maintain human control over assignments. 
•

AI-Driven Developer Assignment | Workflow Orchestrator Project

5. Deep Learning Model Architecture

5.1 Input Features

Feature Category 
Features

Task Features 
Task type, description embedding, required tech stack, priority level, 
estimated complexity

Developer Features 
Skill set vector, years of experience, tech stack match score, current 
workload (active tasks), past performance score

Historical Features 
Number of similar tasks completed, average completion time, 
defect/revision rate on similar tasks

5.2 Model Design

The recommendation system is built as a neural network with the following structure:

• 
Task description processed through a pre-trained BERT embedding or TF-IDF vectorizer to 
create a semantic task vector. 
• 
Developer profile encoded as a numeric feature vector combining skills, experience, workload, 
and historical performance. 
• 
Both vectors are concatenated and passed through a feedforward neural network (FNN) with 3–
4 hidden layers. 
• 
Output layer produces a compatibility score between 0 and 1 for each developer–task pair. 
• 
Developers are ranked by their score and the top candidates are recommended.

5.3 Training Strategy

feedforward neural network (FNN) with 3– 4 hidden layers. • Output layer produces a compatibility score between 0 and 1 for each developer–task pair. • Developers are ranked by their score and the top candidates are recommended. 5.3 Training Strategy … • 
Supervised learning using historical assignment data with outcome labels (successful / delayed 
/ reassigned). 
• 
Loss function: Binary Cross-Entropy or custom weighted loss to penalize poor assignments. 
• 
Optimizer: Adam with learning rate scheduling. 
• 
Periodic retraining triggered after every N new completed tasks to keep the model up to date.

AI-Driven Developer Assignment | Workflow Orchestrator Project

7. Dataset

Since this is an integration into an existing system, the dataset will be built from the Workflow 
Orchestrator's own data:

• 
Historical task assignments — task details, assigned developer, and outcome. 
• 
Developer profiles — skills, years of experience, tech stack, role. 
• 
Performance metrics — task completion times, revision rates, quality scores.

For initial training (cold start), a synthetic dataset will be generated based on defined skill categories and 
common task types. As the system is used, real data will replace synthetic data progressively.

8. Expected Outcomes

times, revision rates, quality scores. For initial training (cold start), a synthetic dataset will be generated based on defined skill categories and common task types. As the system is used, real data will replace synthetic data progressively. 8. Expected Outcomes … • 
A working DL recommendation engine embedded in the Workflow Orchestrator. 
• 
Reduction in task misassignment rates through data-driven suggestions. 
• 
Improved developer utilization by factoring in workload before assignment. 
• 
A self-improving system that gets smarter with each completed task. 
• 
A manager-friendly UI that shows suggestions with confidence scores and reasoning.

9. Scope & Limitations

Scope

• 
The system suggests developers; it does not autonomously assign tasks without manager 
approval. 
• 
Recommendations are limited to developers within the system's registered user base. 
• 
Model performance depends on the quality and volume of historical data available.

Limitations

• 
Cold start problem — the model's early recommendations may be less accurate until sufficient 
real data is collected. 
• 
Does not account for interpersonal or organizational factors that a manager may consider. 
• 
Retraining requires periodic maintenance and computing resources.

10. Conclusion

Integrating a Deep Learning-based developer recommendation system into the Workflow Orchestrator is 
a practical, high-impact enhancement. It brings real AI intelligence into a commonly used project 
management workflow, addressing a genuine pain point of manual task assignment. The system covers 
key DL concepts — NLP, neural networks, feature engineering, and continuous learning — making it 
both a strong academic submission and a genuinely useful software feature. 
The modular design ensures that the DL component can be developed, tested, and deployed 
independently without disrupting the existing orchestrator functionality.

Project: AuroraBoard – A Collaborative Productivity Platform

Introduction

AuroraBoard is a modern full-stack web application designed to enhance team productivity 
through collaborative task management, real-time updates, and intuitive user experiences. This 
document focuses exclusively on the client-side architecture, design decisions, and user 
interaction flows implemented using React.

The frontend is built to be responsive, scalable, and user-centric, ensuring seamless interaction 
across devices while maintaining performance and accessibility standards.

Application Overview

AuroraBoard enables users to create projects, manage tasks, collaborate with team members, 
and track progress through dynamic dashboards. The client-side application acts as the 
interface between users and backend services, handling rendering, state management, and 
user interactions.

Key capabilities include:

• 
Real-time task updates

• 
Drag-and-drop task organization

• 
Role-based UI rendering

• 
Interactive dashboards and analytics

• 
Secure authentication flows

Frontend Architecture

The application follows a component-driven architecture, where the UI is divided into 
reusable and independent components. This ensures maintainability and scalability as the 
project grows.

The architecture is structured into the following layers:

1. Presentation Layer

Responsible for rendering UI components and handling user interactions. Components are 
designed to be reusable and follow a consistent design language.

2. State Management Layer

Handles application-wide state such as user data, authentication status, and project 
information. It ensures that changes in data are reflected across all relevant components 
efficiently.

3. Service Layer

be reusable and follow a consistent design language. 2. State Management Layer Handles application-wide state such as user data, authentication status, and project information. It ensures that changes in data are reflected across all relevant components efficiently. 3. Service Layer … Acts as a bridge between the frontend and backend APIs. It manages data fetching, request 
handling, and error management.

4. Routing Layer

Controls navigation within the application, enabling seamless transitions between pages such 
as dashboards, project views, and user settings.

User Interface Design

AuroraBoard’s UI is designed with a focus on clarity, usability, and responsiveness.

Design Principles

• 
Minimalism: Avoid clutter to improve focus and usability

• 
Consistency: Uniform styling across components

• 
Responsiveness: Optimized for desktop, tablet, and mobile devices

• 
Accessibility: Adherence to accessibility standards for inclusive usage

Layout Structure

• 
Sidebar Navigation: Provides access to projects, dashboards, and settings

• 
Top Bar: Displays notifications, search functionality, and user profile

• 
Main Workspace: Dynamic area where content such as task boards and analytics are 
displayed

Core Features

1. Authentication and User Management

The client-side handles secure login and registration flows, including:

• 
Session persistence

• 
Token-based authentication handling

• 
Conditional rendering based on user roles

Users experience smooth transitions between authenticated and unauthenticated states 
without unnecessary page reloads.

2. Project and Task Management

Users can:

• 
Create and manage multiple projects

• 
Add, edit, and delete tasks

• 
Assign tasks to team members

• 
Organize tasks using drag-and-drop interfaces

The UI updates dynamically to reflect changes instantly, enhancing user experience.

3. Real-Time Collaboration

Users can: • Create and manage multiple projects • Add, edit, and delete tasks • Assign tasks to team members • Organize tasks using drag-and-drop interfaces The UI updates dynamically to reflect changes instantly, enhancing user experience. 3. Real-Time Collaboration … AuroraBoard supports real-time updates, allowing multiple users to interact with the same 
project simultaneously. Changes made by one user are reflected instantly for others, ensuring 
synchronization across sessions.

4. Dashboard and Analytics

The dashboard provides insights into:

• 
Task completion rates

• 
Project progress

• 
Team performance

Interactive visual elements help users quickly understand their workflow and productivity.

State Management Strategy

The application uses a centralized state management approach to ensure consistency across 
components.

Key Characteristics

• 
Global state for shared data such as user information and projects

• 
Local state for component-specific interactions

• 
Efficient updates to minimize unnecessary re-renders

This hybrid approach balances performance with maintainability.

Routing and Navigation

The application implements a structured routing system that enables:

• 
Seamless navigation between pages

• 
Protected routes for authenticated users

• 
Lazy loading of components to improve performance

Users can navigate the platform without full page reloads, ensuring a smooth experience.

Performance Optimization

To ensure optimal performance, several strategies are implemented:

• 
Lazy loading of components to reduce initial load time

• 
Memoization to prevent unnecessary re-renders

• 
Efficient data fetching to minimize API calls

• 
Responsive rendering for different device sizes

These optimizations collectively enhance speed and usability.

Error Handling and User Feedback

The client-side application provides clear and actionable feedback to users:

• 
Inline validation messages for form inputs

• 
Toast notifications for actions and errors

• 
Graceful fallback UI in case of failures

Security Considerations

Security is a key focus in the client-side design:

• 
Secure handling of authentication tokens

• 
Prevention of unauthorized access through protected views

•

Sensitive operations are carefully managed to maintain data integrity.

Accessibility and Responsiveness

AuroraBoard is built with inclusivity in mind:

• 
Keyboard navigability for all interactive elements

• 
Screen reader compatibility

• 
Responsive layouts for various screen sizes

This ensures the application is usable by a wide range of users.

Future Enhancements

Planned improvements for the client-side include:

• 
Offline support with local data caching

• 
Enhanced real-time collaboration features

• 
Customizable dashboards

• 
AI-powered task recommendations

These enhancements aim to further improve usability and productivity.

Conclusion

AuroraBoard’s client-side architecture demonstrates a balance between performance, 
scalability, and user experience. By leveraging modern React principles and thoughtful design 
practices, the application delivers a responsive and intuitive interface for collaborative work.

The modular structure ensures that the frontend can evolve alongside future requirements, 
making it a robust foundation for long-term development.
